post.description: Returns the access token; the refresh token is set in an HttpOnly cookie that is sent only to /api/v1/auth. With two-factor authentication on, unless the device is trusted, returns twoFactorChallenge instead, to exchange with a code at /api/v1/auth/login/two-factor. Native apps (header X-WebWallet-Client) get the refresh token in refreshToken instead of the cookie and send it in the body. Native apps send trustedDeviceToken in the body.

post.description: Exchanges the challenge of the login response and a code of the authenticator app or a recovery code for a session. A wrong code keeps the challenge until it expires; an expired one fails with TWO_FACTOR_EXPIRED. With trustDevice the browser gets a cookie that skips the code for a while. Native apps (header X-WebWallet-Client) get the refresh token in refreshToken instead of the cookie and send it in the body. Native apps get the trusted device as trustedDeviceToken in the body.
post.summary: Finish signing in with a two-factor code

post.description: Succeeds without a token or with an unknown one as well. Native apps (header X-WebWallet-Client) get the refresh token in refreshToken instead of the cookie and send it in the body.
